newsitem.title: INDIA: Police fire on crowd in India, killing at least 5.
newsitem.headline: Police fire on crowd in India, killing at least 5.

text.p: Police fired on a crowd of irate cement workers in central India on Thursday, killing at least five people and injuring six seriously, authorities said.

Sadhna K.K. Singh, a senior official in Madhya Pradesh state, said police opened fire because the mob of nearly 3,000 workers, demanding the arrest of the killers of a union leader, had gone on a rampage in Mehar town.

Singh said the workers were demanding the arrest of the murderers of Ramesh Tiwari, who was killed on May 27 in Mehar, located about 350 km (220 miles) from the state capital Bhopal. She said the crowd damaged property at Mehar police station before police fired in the air, then at the workers.
"In all, 35 rounds were fired off, 25 of which were in the air," she said.
Vikram Verma, an opposition leader in the Madhya Pradesh assembly, said the death toll was much higher. "My information is 11 persons died while 22 were injured," he told Reuters.
Verma said police had fired in haste and demanded a judicial probe.
